summary.oneLiner: and, the metric management insists on

one-line thesis: A standout quarter: revenue Rs 1,509 cr (+27% YoY), PAT Rs 71.51 cr (+43%), and — the metric management insists on — EBITDA/wheel jumped to Rs 314 (from Rs 262), driven largely by long-fought OEM input-price increases finally flowing through ("+1% on margins," with more to come). SSWL is riding a structural domestic up-cycle (GST cuts turbocharging tractors + reviving even the "declining" steel-wheel business) while its export engine turns after two tariff-hit years (June exports +7% YoY, first rise in 2 years, now on a level playing field with Vietnam/Thailand at 10% tariff). All plants run >95% utilization; the Bhuj aluminium wheel (1.2 mn) + knuckles (1.1 mn) plants and a Rs 150 cr agri/PV steel brownfield are being built into a sold-out order book. FY27 guidance: 20%+ top line (~Rs 6,500 cr), ~Rs 650 cr EBITDA, EBITDA/wheel >Rs 310–315, exports ~Rs 600 cr.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | Q1FY27 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | Rs 1,509 cr | +27% | ~Rs 6,000 cr run-rate; healthy across alloy/tractor/CV |
| EBITDA (incl. other income) | Rs 165.17 cr | +32% | margin +40 bps |
| **EBITDA / wheel** | Rs 314 (vs Rs 262 YoY) | +Rs 52 | mgmt's preferred metric — "cleanest way," strips RM-price distortion |
| PAT | Rs 71.51 cr | +43% | PAT margin 4.7% (from sub-5%, targeting 6%) |
| Exports (revenue) | Rs 127 cr | down YoY (Rs 160 cr) but **+37% QoQ** | June +7% YoY — first export rise in 2 years |
| Borrowings | ~Rs 826 cr (LT+ST) | ~flat | interest 8–9%; + factoring limits Rs 400–500 cr |
| Segment mix | Alloy 35% · Truck+Tractor 34% · Knuckles 2% | — | value-added ~70% of revenue |
> EBITDA-% (10.7% area) is deliberately de-emphasized: management repeatedly warns raw-material-price volatility distorts the percentage ("at 10.7% I may be making more money than at 11%") — track **absolute EBITDA and EBITDA/wheel** instead. Aluminium RM cost spiked ~Rs 150 cr in the quarter (passed on to customers, but working-capital lag — explains elevated factoring). Margin drivers: OEM input increases (ex-RM), operating leverage (all plants >95% util), favourable mix (premium/alloy), cost optimization.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Top-line growth:** **20%+** FY27; target ~**Rs 6,500 cr** (~25% on run-rate).
- **EBITDA/wheel:** from Rs 262 (FY26) to **>Rs 310–315** through FY27; **upside bias on Rs 314** (review after Q2).
- **Absolute EBITDA:** ~**Rs 650 cr** FY27 (on ~Rs 6,500 cr revenue).
- **Exports:** ~**Rs 600 cr** FY27; then aim **20%+ growth** thereafter (long-run: exports > domestic within 10 years).
- **Knuckles revenue:** **Rs 110–130 cr** FY27 — roughly **doubling** YoY.
- **Alloy mix:** ~**35–37%** of revenue.
- **Bhuj plants:** alloy wheel 1.2 mn/yr + knuckles 1.1 mn/yr → aluminium segment ~**6.2 mn wheels**; **trial production Q4 FY27**.
- **Agri/PV steel brownfield:** ~**Rs 150 cr**, steel capacity **24 mn → 26 mn**, commercialize **before end of CY2026** (Q4 FY27).
- **Total FY27 capex:** ~**Rs 600 cr** (Bhuj Rs 420 cr + replacement Rs 80 cr + agri brownfield Rs 150 cr, split over FY27/FY28).
- **New-capacity utilization:** ≥**80% by Q1 FY28** (knuckles earlier).
- **PAT margin:** trajectory toward **6%** (from 4.7%) via volume + margin.
order book & pipeline: Not a classic order-book business, but demand visibility is exceptional: **all business units >95% utilization**; knuckles at **100%** with the Bhuj order book "almost completely sold out" before commissioning. Export OEM awards (non-US geographies — Europe, Latin America) ramping over the next 3 quarters. New-customer nominations continuing. Management describes a "structural boom" in CV (3–5 yr run) and tractor/agri (10–15 yr, GST-cut driven) — capacity, not demand, is the constraint.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Alloy (aluminium) wheels — 35%:** strongest growth driver; domestic leadership; only ~2 serious players; SSWL commands a price premium in select cases as the "technically superior" producer. Domestic alloy margins "crashing" (competitors pricing below cost) — SSWL's answer is export diversification, not a price war ("we are not in the cash-burning business").
- **Aluminium knuckles — 2%:** Rs ~23 cr this quarter; running at 100% utilization; 2 customers (started with Mahindra EV program, added a second); FY27 revenue guided Rs 110–130 cr (doubling); export traction expected in 12–18 months.
- **Truck + Tractor — 34%:** tractor strong (rural recovery, higher-HP mechanization, GST-cut affordability); truck a small "blip" last month (monsoon) but structural CV boom intact (replacement + infra + freight).
- **Steel wheels (the reversal):** long-called a "declining business," now growing post-GST-cuts; pass-car steel guided >5% growth; industry "sold out of capacity" — driving the Rs 150 cr agri/PV steel brownfield.
- **Exports:** diversified across Europe/Latin America; tariff drag stabilized (10%, level playing field vs Vietnam/Thailand); June +7% YoY.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Bhuj aluminium complex** (alloy 1.2 mn + knuckles 1.1 mn) with technical partner **Arays** — aftermarket + OEM, predominantly **export-facing**; a global-player ambition ("dominant player of aluminium wheels in the world").
- **Aluminium knuckles into exports** — OEMs already know SSWL's capability from alloy wheels; 12–18-month ramp.
- **Hot stamping** — under discussion for existing OEM relationships (chassis/body lightweighting adjacency).
- **Agri-wheel brownfield** — fungible line (agri + passenger-car steel), +up to 2 mn wheels, hedged growth.
- **Export > domestic** — explicit 10-year strategic goal.
6a. moat & competitive position (optiona:
- **Lowest-cost producer ex-China:** MD asserts "80–90% true… ex-China, hands down, lowest-cost producer" — the structural edge letting SSWL win exports on a level tariff field and refuse below-cost domestic pricing.
- **Aluminium-wheel duopoly + technical premium:** only ~2 serious players; SSWL's technical superiority earns a price premium in select cases and insulates margins as it pivots volume to exports.
- **Back-to-back aluminium pass-through:** moved from quarterly to **monthly** settlement during the West Asia crisis — 30-day lag matched to supplier lag, making SSWL "fully insulated on both downside and upside" of aluminium prices (a hard-won contractual moat vs the prior regime where it "would have lost millions of crores").
- **OEM input-price increases secured:** two years of pushing yielded 1–5% increases (more pending) — pricing power evidenced, not asserted.
margins & cost dynamics: Margin expansion (+40 bps, EBITDA/wheel Rs 262 → Rs 314) is driven by: (1) OEM input-price increases ex-RM (the single biggest lever, ">1% on margins," more to flow); (2) operating leverage at >95% utilization; (3) premium/alloy mix; (4) cost optimization + AI-led labour productivity. Management insists on **EBITDA/wheel over EBITDA-%** because volatile RM prices (aluminium +Rs 150 cr this quarter) distort the ratio. Aluminium is a genuine pass-through (monthly settlement, back-to-back neutral). Manpower issues of the prior year "fully resolved." PAT margin 4.7%, guided toward 6% on volume + margin.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- **Bhuj (greenfield):** alloy wheel 1.2 mn + knuckles ~0.6 mn (this-year phase; 1.1 mn total capacity) = ~Rs 420 cr; **trial production Q4 FY27**; ≥80% utilization by Q1 FY28 (knuckles earlier).
- **Replacement / other plant capex:** ~Rs 80 cr.
- **Agri/PV steel brownfield (Chandigarh mother plant):** ~Rs 150 cr; steel capacity 24 → 26 mn; **commercialize before end CY2026 (Q4 FY27)**; spend split FY27/FY28.
- **Total FY27 capex:** ~Rs 600 cr ±.
- Watch: Q4 FY27 is a crowded commissioning window (Bhuj trial + agri brownfield both land in Q4) — monitor for slippage; further aluminium/knuckles expansion only "on drawing board," gated on export profile over next 3–6 months.
capital allocation: Heavy growth-capex phase (~Rs 600 cr) funded on a levered balance sheet: borrowings ~Rs 826 cr (8–9%) + Rs 400–500 cr factoring limits (used for working-capital spikes, e.g. the Rs 150 cr aluminium RM surge). An analyst explicitly suggested an equity raise to "lighten the balance sheet" for minority shareholders — management noted without commitment. No buyback/dividend detail. Capital is going almost entirely into aluminium (wheels + knuckles) and steel agri/PV capacity where SSWL "strongly dominates."
risks & watch-items:
- **Balance-sheet leverage:** Rs 826 cr debt + Rs 400–500 cr factoring during a Rs 600 cr capex year; working-capital swings on volatile aluminium prices; equity-raise suggestion unanswered.
- **Domestic alloy margin war:** competitors pricing "below cost" — SSWL insulated via exports/premium but domestic alloy margins "crashing."
- **Commissioning concentration:** Bhuj trial + agri brownfield both target Q4 FY27 — execution/slippage risk.
- **West Asia war + commodity volatility:** repeatedly flagged; aluminium price swings (mitigated by monthly pass-through).
- **Tariff / export dependence:** stabilized at 10% level field but "not fully gone away"; export recovery thesis hinges on it holding.
- **EV-program uncertainty:** knuckles seeded on Mahindra's EV program — EV-market "ups and downs" a swing factor (mitigated by second customer + new awards).
- **Truck-segment softness:** monsoon-linked "blip"; management expects post-monsoon buoyancy.
- **China/Arays dependence:** Bhuj aftermarket capability leans on Chinese technical partner Arays.
management quality / tone: Highly confident, promotional, and unusually candid on the "bull run I've never seen in 30–40 years." MD Dheeraj Garg is emphatic on his framework (EBITDA/wheel over EBITDA-%, absolute over percentage) and pushed back firmly on an analyst's "steel is a laggard" premise. He was self-aware about conservatism ("I was being conservative… it exceeded my expectations") and disciplined on not over-guiding ("I don't want to jump the gun… next quarter I'll talk again"). Notably transparent about competitive dynamics (only 2 alloy players, below-cost competition) yet guarded on proprietary detail (steel-vs-alloy EBITDA split deferred to next call; Bhuj/Arays specifics withheld from competitors). Tone: bullish, execution-confident, shareholder-aware (acknowledged the equity-raise suggestion).
non-obvious takeaways:
- **The margin jump is pricing, not just mix:** management is explicit that EBITDA/wheel Rs 262 → Rs 314 is mostly two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1–5%, more pending) — a durable, contracted step-up, not a cyclical mix fluke.
- **Steel wheels flipped from structural decliner to growth engine** post-GST-cuts — a genuine narrative reversal (industry "sold out of capacity," 15–20 years of pass-car-steel problems "come to an end") that justifies the Rs 150 cr agri/PV brownfield.
- **Track absolute EBITDA + EBITDA/wheel, ignore EBITDA-%** — the single most repeated instruction; RM-price volatility makes the percentage actively misleading (higher RM can mean more money at a lower %).
- **Aluminium is de-risked to a pure pass-through** — the shift to monthly settlement makes SSWL "back-to-back neutral," so aluminium-price headlines should not scare on margins.
- **Capacity, not demand, is the binding constraint** — knuckles at 100%, all units >95%, Bhuj "sold out" pre-commissioning; the investable question is execution/commissioning timing (Q4 FY27), not order intake.
- **Export-over-domestic is the real long-game** — SSWL wants exports > domestic within 10 years, using India's low-cost base; domestic alloy price war is being sidestepped, not fought.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.

themes.title: Auto OEM cycle - CV replacement & PV premiumization
themes.need: GST 2.0 rate rationalization plus an aged CV fleet still frames the replacement cycle, but Q1FY27's real signal is 2W OEMs EXPANDING margin through a commodity shock. TVSMOTOR sold 1.63mn units (+28%) on INR 13,896cr revenue (+38%) while lifting EBITDA margin 30bps to 12.8% having absorbed a ~4% commodity shock with only ~1.5% of price increase (CARE upgraded it AA+ to AAA), and committed 2W capacity from 6.8mn to 8.3mn by Q4FY27. BAJAJ-AUTO set volume/revenue/EBITDA records with margin at 20.9% (+110bps) through ~4.5% commodity inflation AND ~10% of volume lost to a ransomware shutdown, with EV now 30% of domestic revenue at double-digit EBITDA and Chetak EBITDA-positive - a scaled, profitable EV second engine. Commercial mobility is electrifying fastest: TVSMOTOR's 3W EV penetration crossed 40% for the first time. ASHOKLEY's all-time-high CV volumes (220k units, MHCV share 30.8%) carry the CV leg with defence + Switch EV optionality; TMCV/TMPV/SMLMAH/ESCORTS on CV/tractors; APOLLOTYRE/JKTYRE/BALKRISIND/MRF on tyres.
themes.driver: Capacity commissioning against demand (TVSMOTOR 2W to 8.3mn by Q4FY27, BAJAJ-AUTO 7m to 9m+ units); 3W/2W EV penetration inflection; GST-2.0 price-cut demand, aged-fleet replacement and festive 2W/PV.
